She said many times, speaking of her daughter: «This was the punishment for my sins». The very particular condition of the mute daughter must be stressed. It was this misfortune of hers that made her very inclined toward her daughter and hers.

Ad 29: In the exercise of all the aforesaid virtues the Servant of God certainly did not exceed; she was just and balanced. She was an agreeable Saint.

§ 378
Fortitude and serenity of the Servant of God in her last illness.

Ad 33, Proc. fol. 1267: The Servant of God began to worsen after the feast of St. Anne of 1899. After this feast, having stopped at Pisa on the journey and been examined by the doctor, he, astonished, said to the Sisters present: «But how do you manage to carry this woman around? She is no longer fit to travel». She then went on to Sampierdarena, to visit that house, and another, at Sestri Ponente.

The breathlessness and the swelling of the abdomen kept growing. She then went to our house in Genoa in Piazza San Silvestro, where to arrive she had to suffer much because of the uphill stretch that could not be done in a sedan chair. Having at last arrived upstairs, I believe she had a fainting fit, or she then became so much worse that, alarming the Sisters, they telegraphed me to send our Doctor Montechiari at once, who, however, did not leave, because a subsequent telegram announced that it was not urgent. We were all alarmed, and here and in all the houses prayers were said. She then recovered, enough to set out on the journey to Rome, accompanied, however, by the doctor and, I think, also by a Priest. Here, after being in bed for a little while, she recovered somewhat. And I remember that she took great pains in giving orders for the episcopal consecration of Mgr. Di Belmonte. About that time she made her will. The one who saw to it that she made a will was the Apostolic Visitor, Mgr. Di Belmonte, and to some extent the Secretaries.

It was Cardinal Rampolla who, in our adjoining Church, consecrated Mgr. Di Belmonte, and the Servant of God took advantage of this circumstance to beg the Cardinal to accept the Protectorship of our Institute. The prayers of the newly consecrated were added too, and in the end the Cardinal (though, I believe, not on that day) was induced to accept. In January the Servant of God was struck by influenza, which reduced her ever worse, although she overcame that illness too.

Despite all these ailments, the Servant of God occupied herself ceaselessly with her Institute, gave orders, received and wrote letters. Having thus reached the third of May, that morning, when she came into the study, where I too was with others of the Secretariat, she made on all the most painful impression by the extraordinary pallor of her face. She sat down as usual on a chair at her table, occupying herself even then with the affairs of her Institute. After dinner she felt so ill that they had to carry her to bed. The doctor, called, as soon as he saw her, said it was peritonitis and that it was over. Professor Marchiafava was also called, I do not know whether the same day, who would have liked to examine her carefully, but the Servant of God, who did not want to be touched by anyone, as she had never been touched by Doctor Montechiari, did not allow it: which irritated Marchiafava somewhat, so that he went so far as to reproach her. At night, toward morning, she made her Communion, though not fasting, given the permission she had. The next day she grew ever worse, and I recall that she wished to get out of bed to go near the little Madonna which the Ven. Clausi always carried in his hand, and which had been brought to her by Fr. Donadio, Postulator of the Cause of that Venerable.

§ 379
She received with great fervor the last spiritual aids.

On the fifth, growing ever worse, she was exhorted by Fr. Donadio and by Fr. Vincenzo to receive the Holy Oil, and she answered: «So be it».

In the morning, very early, of that day she had received Holy Communion as Viaticum. The Holy Oil having been administered to her, she settled on one side, looking from time to time at her Crucifix and her little Madonna (that of the Ven. Clausi) which were before her eyes, and spoke no more.

§ 380
Holy death, funeral and burial.

That night, from the fifth to the sixth, we were present, all the Sisters, Fr. Agostino Donadio, Fr. Vincenzo d'Alatri, Sr. Amante La Barbera, those of her family who came and went, except her brother Federico, who did not stir until her death. On the sixth, the day of the Consecration of our Church, while the bells were ringing, at nine fifteen in the morning she breathed her last.

Many Superiors of our Houses arrived from elsewhere, some neighboring Communities and other persons came to see the body of the Servant of God and to pray, and those who came said: «A Saint has died», and touched her body with rosaries and medals.

Ad 34: The Sisters who dressed the Servant of God said they had found on her body the marks of the little chains, of the hair shirts and other instruments of penance which the Mother had used. After her death, when I saw the Crucifix with a little flesh adhering and which had been driven into her side, as I was told, I then explained to myself why so many times, speaking with her, one noticed a certain odor which was not bad or disgusting, but which made one believe that a wound had formed in her side.

The Sisters who dressed her were the present Provincial of Ovada, Sr. Anna Consolata Massinelli, the Mistress of Novices of that time, now deceased, Sr. Anna Serafina Foglia, and I do not remember others. The clothes of the Servant of God were collected by Mother Carrega, and many asked her for some little piece out of devotion.

The body was placed in three coffins, I think, of wood, of lead and of walnut. I recall that on Monday it was carried to the chapel adjoining this hall, where it remained all night; and on Tuesday morning it was carried into the Church, where everything was ready for the funeral. Many people attended it, even uninvited, and the Church was full. There were many poor, who showed their gratitude to their Benefactress, and also Gentlemen.

Ad 35: At the funeral procession to the Cemetery there was a great quantity of people, the street was full; there were very many of our Sisters, come from elsewhere, who showed their desolation. To us Sisters it seemed that everything was over with the death of our Mother.

I must note that at the funeral and the procession of the Servant of God all the Barbiellini were absent.

At the Cemetery she was laid in our tomb in the quadriporticus, whence she was taken the following year in March and placed in our sepulchre at the Pincetto in Campo Verano. Our sepulchre consists of four levels. In the upper part there is the Chapel and over the door of the Chapel is the tomb of the Servant of God: I do not remember the epigraph.

§ 381
Reputation for holiness and graces received.

Ad 36: I recall that to her tomb were brought by various private persons garlands with the inscription «for grace received», not, however, silver ex votos.

Ad 37: I go rarely to the tomb of the Servant of God, and on those few occasions I found no one. I know that the Princess of Fitalia, every time she comes to Rome, always goes there, has Masses celebrated, prays and obtains what she wants through her intercession.

Ad 38: All those who knew the Servant of God, and our Sisters in general, hold her in great esteem and believe that one day she will be venerated on the altars, whether for the virtues with which she showed herself adorned in this life, or also for the fruits her Institute has borne.

I leave aside, naturally, frivolous persons, and as to the opinion of which I spoke before, I have heard it spoken of only by serious persons.

Among these persons worthy of note, Mrs. Frascara, who called our Sisters to Sezzè in Piedmont, where she went for her summer holidays (now deceased); Mgr. Scalabrini, Bishop of Piacenza. Certainly many others held her in extraordinary esteem, but I do not know whether as a saint of the altar.

To form this general opinion there was certainly no artifice on our part, but it arose naturally, and from the reputation of the virtues she exercised in life.

D. Donato of S. Maria di Capua Vetere, who was once seen to rise in the air here in our Chapel; Brother Agatangelo of the Friars Minor, who enjoyed a reputation for holiness, said with our Sisters that the Servant of God was a Saint; and so many others whose names I do not remember.

Et expleto examine super Interrogatoriis, interrogata fuit Testis supra Articulis, super quibus, (Proc. fol. 1277) respondit: se nihil aliud praeter ea, quae deposuit super Interrogatoriis, sed addidit sequentia:

p. 227

Do not think that the things I have said in praise of Mother Gattorno were said by me because I was well treated and fondled by her, but only out of the veneration I have for her memory. I, from Mother Gattorno, although I had delicate offices, as I have already deposed, did not lack grave pains from her; pains that made me weep several times, and to hide my weeping I took refuge in a secluded place.

Once, without her telling me the reason (I did not ask it and still do not know it), she transferred me from Superior of this Generalate house to that of Genoa, always as Superior. Sometimes she reproached me, telling me that I lacked poverty. Also when I was transferred to Florence I felt much pain; I accepted, however, all the pains that came to me from the hand of the Servant of God as permission of the Lord, and never on that account diminished my esteem and veneration toward our Mother.
